articles.title: Eagles sign QB Joe Milton from Cowboys' practice squad with Jalen Hurts out
articles.summary: Hurts is set to miss this week after a blood clot was found in his leg.
articles.body:
With starting quarterback Jalen Hurts out for Week 6 (and possibly beyond) , the Philadelphia Eagles are turning elsewhere to pad their QB room. The Eagles are signing third-year QB Joe Milton off the Dallas Cowboys' practice squad, according to multiple reports.

Under NFL rules, Milton will join Philadelphia's 53-man roster, rather than the Eagles' practice squad, after being signed.

Hurts was ruled out for Sunday's matchup against the Carolina Panthers after a superficial blood clot was found in his leg. He is set to undergo treatment, but it's unclear whether he will have to miss more time after this Sunday; however, the addition of Milton seems to indicate that Hurts may be out for longer than just this week.

Milton, who was selected by the New England Patriots in the sixth round of the 2024 draft, will now be on his third team in less than three seasons. He has taken limited snaps in five games across the past two seasons, and has yet to get a start in the NFL.

The signing also marks an unusual transaction between the Eagles and the Cowboys, who are longtime NFC East rivals.

Milton will join backup QB Tanner McKee and rookie Cole Payton in Philadelphia's QB room, likely entering Sunday's game as the third-string quarterback. McKee, a former 2023 sixth-round pick, is expected to get the start against the Panthers.

It will be just the third start for the 26-year-old McKee, who has played in just six games across the past two seasons with the Eagles. McKee's last start came in Week 18 of last season, with the backup giving Hurts a rest before the postseason; McKee was sacked three times and threw an interception in an eventual 24-17 loss to the Washington Commanders.

articles.title: Broncos' Jonathon Cooper Eligible to Return from NFL Exempt List for Week 7 vs. Cardinals
articles.summary: The NFL removed Denver Broncos linebacker Jonathon Cooper from the Commissioner Exempt List on Friday.
articles.body:
The NFL removed Denver Broncos linebacker Jonathon Cooper from the Commissioner Exempt List on Friday.

Cooper will be eligible to make his season debut during the Broncos' Week 7 matchup with the Arizona Cardinals on Oct. 25.

He was initially placed on the Commissioner's Exempt list on Aug. 30 and was barred from practicing or attending the team's games before he was reinstated.

Cooper is entering his sixth season as a member of the Broncos after they selected him with a seventh-round pick in the 2021 NFL draft.

He wrapped up a 2025 campaign in which he recorded 50 tackles, 16 quarterback hits, eight sacks and four passes defended in 17 games. The 28-year-old has amassed at least eight sacks in each of the past three years.

After advancing to the AFC Championship Game last season, the Broncos have opened 2026 with a 4-2 record. They're coming off a 17-14 overtime win over the Seattle Seahawks on Thursday night.

The Broncos still own one of the NFL's top defensive units this year, ranking No. 9 among all teams by allowing 20.8 points per game.

Kickoff between Denver and Arizona on Oct. 25 is at 4:05 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Inside the NFL game management world tasked with preventing snafus like Commanders just had: 'It's irresponsible not to learn from others' mistakes'
articles.summary: Game-management coordinators typically speak more on the gameday headset than their position-coach colleagues. But it's not an exact science, as the Commande...
articles.body:
In an ideal world, the Washington Commanders would have had The Conversation before their last drive.

We have no timeouts. We can't take a sack. We need an out-of-bounds or end-zone play that sets up our kicker at his preferred hash.

In this ideal world, the Commanders would have already circulated end-of-game situational awareness through training camp and, to some degree, throughout practice and game-planning during the week. They'd have assessed their time cutoffs during training camp to understand how long several of their plays and operational considerations take, knowing precisely what they need to bleed the clock but still leave time for a spike and field-goal attempt.

And after all that had happened, in this ideal world, head coach Dan Quinn would have directed offensive coordinator David Blough before the Commanders' overtime two-minute drive what the team's yardage and play-clock threshold was to set up a field goal for a kicker who had already missed an extra point that day. Before the play that QB Jayden Daniels ultimately snapped with 12 seconds left, Quinn — perhaps aided by his game management staffers — would have reminded Blough the time cutoff for a spike, Blough would have reminded Daniels he can't take a sack and has no timeouts, and Daniels (perhaps running a play-call that didn't involve a personnel substitution and take more time) would have reminded teammates the situation. Daniels and teammates would have kicked into urgency mode to get the last spike off.

The Commanders still might have missed the kick. But perhaps they would have avoided the operational fiasco that triggered Quinn slamming his headset, part team owner Magic Johnson tweeting he was "in total disbelief my Commanders had such poor clock management," and Daniels telling his teammates of the missed chance that left the Commanders tied with the New York Giants: "It'll never happen again."

How many of these ideal steps happened? It's near impossible to know. But seeing the play triggered coaches and game-management coordinators around the league who know how much has to go right in those situations — and how colleagues' jobs and legacies are on the line.

"There are still paths to victory with basically every decision you make," one game management coordinator told Yahoo Sports. "Everyone wants to point fingers and blame one thing and it's not that simple. …

The Commanders' operational failure spotlighted the role of game management coordinators across the NFL, a group whose jobs help prevent these very snafus from happening.

But how does the process work? How do NFL teams manage game clocks, communicate on headsets and respond to the unexpected in real time? Yahoo Sports spoke to game management coordinators from six NFL teams as well as two former offensive coordinators to better understand. All except former offensive coordinator Scott Turner spoke on condition of anonymity due to concerns about competitive advantage surrounding their team's strategy. (Turner is not currently with an NFL team.) They also emphasized their goal was not to knock the Commanders or other teams with recent late-game struggles, knowing that their own teams and processes have each failed at one point or another.

And yet, "it's irresponsible not to learn from other people's mistakes — and from your own," one game management coordinator said.

So teams are discussing where the Commanders fell short and how to prevent a repeat.

"The fact that it's been so publicized, I think most of the teams are probably having more conversations about it," another game management coordinator said. "But in my opinion, the really good situational teams have already been having those conversations."

What do NFL game-management coordinators do?

Determining with certainty how many teams have an official game management coordinator is complicated. Titles vary dramatically from one game-management staffer to the next, some teams not even sharing publicly who runs this proprietary role for them. But a Yahoo Sports analysis of NFL media guides, LinkedIn profiles and conversations with coaches in the league identified 21 teams with a game-management role on their coaching staff and 11 teams who have tabbed a front office member to oversee responsibilities.

Roles differ among game-management coordinators but tend to start in the same place: managing timeouts; guiding decisions on when to go for it on fourth downs or 2-point conversion attempts; and establishing thresholds in two-minute play to manipulate the clock. From there, roles at times expand to helping head coaches determine when to accept or reject a penalty, devising and sequencing plays during the final two minutes of the half or game, and teaching players and coaches about situational moments that influenced games across the league the prior week.

"We have to be flexible," one game-management coordinator said, "because if you're doing stuff that's not hitting their brains, then it's worthless."

Some game-management coordinators present to the team one or more times each week during the season, while others collaborate specifically with the head coach or head coach and coordinators. Gradually, trusted game managers around the league are spending weekday time in the quarterback room given how crucial coach, play-caller and quarterback alignment is in situational, less-repped moments.

"Those three people need to be on the same page," a game-management coordinator said.

Game-management coordinators typically speak more on the gameday headset than their position-coach colleagues, but how active they are on the headset differs, they say. Excelling in the role often requires a keen understanding of coaches' personalities and temperaments.

Game-management staffers assess: Does my play-caller prefer to know the viability of four-down territory after first down or after second? How concisely can I deliver all necessary information when an offensive play-caller is not in conversation with the quarterback and the defensive coordinator not communicating to the "green dot" mic-ed up player? What's the most important information and who needs it? Does my play-caller prefer a constant stream of reminders or primarily quiet to think?

Different coaches warrant different game-management styles.

"I'd much rather get told to shut up on the headset than to not say something and do something stupid out there," one game-management coordinator said.

Added another: "People do freeze up as the clock's ticking down, and there's so many people that have the ability to speak up, but you'll be surprised in those situations how sometimes people defer or they're scared to say something out of turn in a stressful situation.

"You'll be surprised how often it's crickets."

Some head coaches want game-management coordinators talking on the "main" headset lines for offense and defense (and special teams, if the special teams coordinator wears a headset, which not all do) while other head coaches (often non-play callers) prefer a clean line for their game-management coordinator to relay information directly to the head coach, and the head coach to then relay. Sometimes the goal is to inform a decision; other times, to announce it. Guidance will factor in advance scouting of opponents — how does this opponent defend out-of-bounds plays? Hail Marys?

The nuances of weighing odds and influential factors swirl in coaches' heads, but the decision-making goal remains generally the same.

"We're totally just in risk management," a game-management coordinator said.

Recent Cowboys, Eagles losses a reminder that decision making 'not black and white'

Practicing situational periods across training camp and in-season practices is standard for NFL teams. Visit a training camp, and it's rare to see a practice that doesn't include a situational period given how often NFL games come down to the fourth quarter and game-winning drives.

But one game management coordinator estimated the math as such: Imagine a team practices its bread-and-butter plays three to five times a week. Given the variety of situational outcomes, a team is more likely to practice a single type of situation once every two to three weeks (with other situations practiced in the interim).

"I think most teams hit a two-minute drive every week in practice," the coordinator said. "Now, do they have an end-of-game clock situation that comes up? Maybe, maybe not. Definitely not every week. …

"You can only spend so much time for the amount of times it's going to come up in a game. You'd love to rep them all a million times and be perfect at them, but it's not realistic."

The Commanders aren't the only team to cough up a recent game in the final seconds. The Dallas Cowboys tied the Baltimore Ravens with 7 seconds to play in Rio de Janeiro in Week 3. Overtime seemed imminent, and Dallas opted to kick a touchback that set up the Ravens at their own 35-yard line. A defensive gamble followed, Lamar Jackson completing a 27-yard pass to Zay Flowers and then calling a timeout with 1 second left. Ravens kicker Tyler Loop kicked a game-winning 56-yard field goal to secure the 34-31 victory.

Should the Cowboys have forced a return?

"I hurt our chance to win that game," head coach Brian Schottenheimer told reporters afterward.

The Philadelphia Eagles' loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars last Sunday called into question Schottenheimer's statement.

Playing in London, the Eagles kicked a go-ahead field goal with 8 seconds to play. They chose to kick the ball in bounds, seemingly needing just one good stop from their kick-return unit to guarantee victory. Jacksonville running back Ameer Abdullah executed a well-devised and well-blocked 53-yard return, leaving 1 second on the clock. Kicker Cam Little — who holds the NFL record for longest made kick, at 68 yards — connected from 57 yards. Jaguars win 19-17.

The scenarios weren't completely identical. But they were similar, the Cowboys and Ravens opted for opposite strategies, and each lost.

"Having two different outcomes just shows you that it's not black and white," a game-management coordinator said.

And while game-planning is crucial, strategy can only take a team so far, former NFL offensive coordinator Scott Turner told Yahoo Sports.

"At some point, you still have to tackle people, you still have to cover a kickoff," said Turner, who coordinated the Carolina Panthers, Washington Commanders and Las Vegas Raiders offenses in various stints between 2019-24. "The game management stuff [is] all tools. It's information. But you got to block people and you got to tackle people and you got to catch it and you got to run good routes."

The Commanders have their first chance to move forward from their botched end-of-game on Monday, when they face the 5-0 San Francisco 49ers on the road in prime time. The spotlights will be bright. The opponent, by record, more successful.

Throughout the weekend, expect not only the Commanders but every NFL team to dial in on how they prepare for situational football and how they communicate that preparation in the heat of the game. Expect play-callers to await the advice, and the communication, streaming through their headsets.

"Just that overcommunication, making sure everyone's on the same page," a second former offensive coordinator said. "So when all hell's breaking loose, no one's caught off guard."

articles.title: Eagles rule out RB Saquon Barkley (hamstring), WR DeVonta Smith (hamstring) good to go for Week 6 vs. Panthers
articles.summary: Both players missed last week's loss to the Jaguars in London.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles will be without running back Saquon Barkley for the second straight week, but will get wide receiver DeVonta Smith back after a two-game absence.

Barkley will sit out against the Carolina Panthers due to a hamstring injury. After exiting four snaps into Week 4, the running back sat out last week's loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in London.

Smith has not played since Week 3, missing the past two games with his own hamstring issue. He had no injury designation on the Friday injury report.

Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Basketball league for the 2026-27 NBA season

Smith took part in Friday's practice and told reporters afterward he felt "good" and that the decision on his availability for Sunday will be "up to the doctors."

Fellow Eagles wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks was a full participant in practice. He is dealing with a hamstring injury and was limited Wednesday before being held out of practice on Thursday. He returned to the field on Friday.

The Eagles will already be without quarterback Jalen Hurts after doctors found a superficial blood clot in his leg . Tanner McKee is in line to start at QB, though the Eagles signed QB Joe Milton on Friday from the Cowboys practice squad.

After this week, the 2-3 Eagles have three straight games against NFC East rivals beginning next Monday night against the Dallas Cowboys, followed by a Sunday night meeting with the Washington Commanders in Week 8 before returning home to take on the New York Giants. They will take their bye in Week 10.

articles.title: Packers RB Josh Jacobs to be removed from NFL's commissioner exempt list, will be eligible to play Week 7
articles.summary: Jacobs was arrested for domestic abuse last May and was placed on the list ahead of the season. The league says the investigation into Jacobs' conduct is sti...
articles.body:
Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs is being removed from the commissioner exempt list, the NFL announced Friday.

Jacobs had been placed on the list on Aug. 30 after a domestic abuse arrest last May. In Friday's statement, the league said that the investigation into Jacobs' arrest "remains ongoing and is not affected" by Jacobs being removed from the list.

Jacobs will be officially taken off the list on Monday. He will be eligible to make his season debut in Week 7, as the Packers take on the Detroit Lions on Oct. 25.

Jacobs was arrested in northern Wisconsin on May 26 and charged with multiple counts of domestic abuse. The charges stemmed from an incident three days prior, when Jacobs allegedly grabbed a woman trying to leave his garage and threw her to the ground.

Jacobs was formally charged with two of those counts, battery and criminal damage to property, the week before he was placed on the commissioner exempt list. He pleaded no contest to both charges last month.

Jacobs is now trying to prevent evidence, including footage of the incident, from being released publicly: The running back filed a civil suit earlier this week , calling for an injunction and protective order that would restrict access to records in his case. The Brown County district attorney has reportedly said that surveillance footage outside Jacobs' garage corroborates the victim's account of the incident.

In a statement, Jacobs' attorneys, Clarence F. Duchac III, David Z. Chesnoff and Richard A. Schonfeld, said he was "excited to get back to work" after being removed from the list.

"Josh has dedicated the last several months to bettering himself, and he accepts responsibility for his actions," the statement said, via The Ringer's Tom Pelissero . "Josh is grateful for the support he is receiving from his teammates, coaches, the Packers organization, and the greatest fans in the world. Since there are ongoing legal matters, he will not have any further comment."

articles.title: Eagles poach QB from Cowboys amid Jalen Hurts blood clot uncertainty
articles.summary: With QB Jalen Hurts sidelined by a blood clot in his calf, the Philadelphia Eagles are signing an intriguing player from the Dallas Cowboys' practice squad.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles plan to poach a quarterback from an NFC East rival in the wake of Jalen Hurts' unexpected injury .

The Eagles are signing Joe Milton III off the practice squad of the Dallas Cowboys , according to multiple reports on Friday, Oct. 16. This was the start of Milton's second season with the Cowboys after being traded to Dallas by the New England Patriots in exchange for a fifth-round pick in April 2025 .

NFL rules stipulate that a player signed off another team's practice squad must be placed on the 53-man roster. The Eagles are scheduled to host the Carolina Panthers in Week 6 action on Sunday.

Best touchdown celebrations NFL fans won't forget from the 2026 season

How Joe Milton fits with Eagles after Jalen Hurts injury

The Eagles announced on Thursday that Hurts has a "superficial blood clot," that he is believed to have suffered during the team's Oct. 4 game against the Los Angeles Rams . He was cleared to play in Philadelphia's Oct. 11 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in London, England, before a follow-up ultrasound "revealed movement in the small blood clot." That led the Eagles to shut Hurts down for the immediate future.

Before acquiring Milton, back-up Tanner McKee and rookie Cole Payton were the only other quarterbacks listed on the Philadelphia roster. McKee, 26, is slated to be the starter under center in Week 6 for the Eagles. He was the starting quarterback during the final game of the Eagles' regular season in each of the past two years and had a 1-1 record in those appearances. Payton was Philadelphia's fifth-round pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.

If McGee were to falter and Hurts' absence forces an injured reserve stint, Milton could have an opportunity to start some games in Philadelphia. He's long been an intriguing developmental prospect because of his arm strength and could offer a downfield passing element to an offense that has struggled to generate explosive plays.

Milton has never started an NFL game and has five career regular-season appearances over two seasons with the Patriots and Cowboys. Most of Milton's experience has come in the preseason, including several impressive moments in August with Dallas.

Milton completed more than 67% of his passes over three 2026 exhibition games for 378 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions. It included an eye-popping performance in his lone preseason start on Aug. 22 against the Arizona Cardinals in which he completed 9 of 13 passes for 179 yards and accounted for three touchdowns (two passing, one rushing).

He won't be a long-term answer due to inconsistency and accuracy issues that have cropped up throughout his career. But Milton has shown enough promise to become a helpful stopgap until Hurts is back. It's a relatively low-risk move for the Eagles.

articles.title: New Jaguars long snapper cuts camping trip short, scrambles for passport before Sunday's London game
articles.summary: Jacob Bobenmoyer was camping and changing diapers in Colorado when the Jacksonville Jaguars called him to fly to London as their emergency long snapper.
articles.body: Last weekend's game between the Jacksonville Jaguars and Philadelphia Eagles at London's Tottenham Hotspur Stadium was a wild one, and one thing that was a headache for the Jags was the long-snapping situation. Long snapper Ross Matiscik hurt his shoulder, and that meant defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton had to take over. The results were mixed, and one snap on an extra point was so high that it led to a bad hold and a rare miss from that range for kicker Cam Little. But now, while the Jags were staying in London ahead of their game against the Houston Texans at Wembley Stadium, they called in former Broncos and Raiders long snapper Jacob Bobenmoyer. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! It's surely a welcome call, but it tanked his camping trip and had him praying his passport was still in the bathroom drawer he had chucked it in. Bobenmoyer was camping in the wilds of Colorado when he got a text from his agent telling him that the Jags would likely be getting in touch with him. So he headed home on the off chance that they would want him to head to the airport that night, which they did. So imagine being on a camping trip and having to head home early because you've got to wing it on over to London to handle long-snapping duties for the Jaguars. Now, imagine getting that call while "changing diapers and whatnot," which is what happened to Bobenmoyer. What a wild couple of hours. But there was still the matter of the passport in the bathroom drawer, which Bobenmoyer didn't think he'd need again. RAMS CUT KICKER HARRISON MEVIS AFTER BOTCHED FIELD GOAL ATTEMPT IN OVERTIME 'COST US THE GAME' "They called me, and I was like, ‘Man, I hope it’s still there,’" Bobenmoyer said, per the Associated Press. The 29-year-old out of Northern Colorado has 97 NFL games under his belt, spread over three seasons in Denver and another three in Las Vegas. Bobenmoyer hit free agency this past offseason, but crucially, didn't give up after not signing going into the season. Another bite at the NFL apple and a free trip to London. Can't beat it.

articles.title: Dolphins’ 7-round 2027 NFL Draft according to PFF mock draft simulator during bye week
articles.summary: The Miami Dolphins are 0-5 as they head into their bye week, and their chances of getting better this year are slim to none. This is by design, though, as th...
articles.body:
The Miami Dolphins are 0-5 as they head into their bye week, and their chances of getting better this year are slim to none. This is by design, though, as the team took the biggest dead cap hit in league history this season. What Dolphins fans can look forward to is the 2027 NFL Draft , where the 'Phins will have a chance to start their long-awaited rebuild.

Since Miami is sitting out Week 6, it's a good time to look ahead to who could be coming in next season. That's why we asked the PFF 2027 NFL Mock Draft simulator to give us an idea of what April's class could look like.

Round 1, Pick 3: OT Trevor Goosby, Texas

There are two schools of thought here with the Dolphins' first overall pick, which the PFF 2027 NFL Mock Draft simulator predicted to be the third overall selection. The franchise could go with a quarterback or build out everything else first before going and getting a franchise signal-caller.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

With Malik Willis under contract for another season, going with Plan B here makes a lot of sense. The 2027 QB class doesn't seem all it was made out to be, and putting a top-three rookie on the field with the startling lack of talent the Dolphins currently have on the roster is bordering on irresponsible.

Trevor Goosby is a mountain of a man at 6-foot-7, 325 pounds, and looks like he can be a bookend tackle for the next decade-plus in the NFL. The most successful franchises—including the Green Bay Packers, where much of the Miami braintrust hails from—build from the trenches, and getting a potential Pro Bowl left tackle makes a lot of sense.

With the defensive-minded Jeff Hafley as head coach, an elite defensive player like Notre Dame CB Leonard Moore of Texas EDGE Colin Simmons would also make sense, but an LT is a solid move here.

Round 2, Pick 34: WR Reed Harris, Arizona State

The Sun Devils' 6-foot-5, 217-pound pass-catcher, Reed Harris, is climbing up draft boards as he continues to produce results even as Arizona State struggles without Sam Leavitt. He's put up 34 catches for 590 yards and seven touchdowns through five games, and looks more and more like an NFL wideout with each passing contest.

Miami's WR corps is horrific this season, and whether it is Willis or a ookie QB next season, the signal-caller has zero chance of succeeding without some better weapons. Harris is rising up draft boards and looks like a potential WR1, so this would make a ton of sense at the top of Round 2.

Round 3, Pick 65: C Anthony Boswell, Houston

Houston's center is slightly undersized at 6-foot-2, 301 pounds, but he is an excellent blocker who hasn't allowed a sack in almost 500 snaps. Anthony Boswell continues the Dolphins' building from the trenches in this 2027 NFL Mock Draft, which would earn a solid grade from any draft evaluator.

Goosby and Boswell will join Kadyn Proctor, from the 2026 draft, and give Miami three of the five pieces they need for an incredible offensive line. The rest of the current group or any free agents can compete for the other two spots, and the Dolphins could really have something up front sooner rather than later.

Round 4, Pick 101: S Bray Hubbard, Alabama

Bray Hubbard is a do-it-all safety for Alabama who continues to rack up the tackles and the takeaways in college. As a mid-round pick, he will bring versatility and toughness to any defense, which the Dolphins can definitely use. He will also be a great fit for Hafley, who likes to disguise his defenses by moving versatile safeties around the formation.

Round 5, Pick 140: WR Evan Stewart, Oregon

Staying with wide receiver here, the Dolphins get Evan Stewart with their own pick in Round 5, according to the PFF 2027 NFL Mock Draft simulator. Stewart would be a familiar type of pick for Miami and a nice complement for the big-bodied Harris. The Oregon Duck is a speed burner who was, at one point, considered a first or second-round pick. A knee injury has slowed his production a bit, but when he gets fully back, he could be the next Jaylen Waddle.

Round 5, Pick 154: CB Zeke Barry, Michigan

Even at 5-foot-11, 188 pounds, Zeke Barry is not afraid to stick his nose into the fray and make tackles. He is a good cover man and a tough, physical corner. One of his current NFL comps is Jaire Alexander, whom Hafley knows well, having coached him in Green Bay. Drafting the same type of player in Round 5 makes a lot of sense.

Round 6, Pick 34: QB Aidan Chiles, Northwestern

We couldn't get through a Dolphins mock draft without taking at least one QB, could we? At 6-foot-3, 225 pounds, and with a rocket arm and athleticism to burn, Aidan Chiles is incredibly raw but has an intriguingly high ceiling. In fact, he's not all that different from Willis, so taking a project signal-caller like Chiles to sit and learn behind Willis is a smart idea.

Round 7, Pick 34: EDGE Teitum Tuioti, Oregon

Another Hafley-type defender, Teitun Tuioti is a solid run defender and a pass-rusher with upside. At worst, he should be a decent rotational EDGE at the next level, and at best, under his Dolphins head coach, Tuioti could develop into a solid starting edge player.

articles.title: Troy Aikman’s Dolphins consultant role contractually in limbo
articles.summary: Troy Aikman has made it clear in recent days that his time with ESPN might be ending when his contract expires in March. His Miami Dolphins consultancy role...
articles.body:
Troy Aikman has made it clear in recent days that his time with ESPN might be ending when his contract expires in March.

His Miami Dolphins consultancy role also appears to be up in the air.

According to Mark Maske of Front Office Sports, Aikman does not have a "formal and ongoing agreement" with the Dolphins regarding his formal advisory role as a consultant to the NFL club.

"It's not known to what extent, if at all, Aikman continues to advise the Dolphins based on his relationships with owner Stephen Ross, coach Jeff Hafley, and general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan," wrote Maske. "But if that's occurring, it's not a formal arrangement, according to the source, who told FOS that Aikman's official consulting role with the Dolphins was limited to the team's searches that resulted in the hirings of Sullivan and Hafley this past offseason."

It's unclear if Aikman was planning on continuing that role following this NFL season, though the league did announce that he would face similar restrictions as those placed on Tom Brady , limiting his direct access to teams, players, and coaches in the week leading up to the Monday Night Football game he would be calling. While he remains eligible to broadcast games involving the Dolphins, the NFL's tampering and gambling policies very much apply to him.

Aikman griped that the restrictions were unnecessary , since they didn't create a conflict of interest, while admitting the Dolphins hired him for his unique access to information as a broadcaster .

As for how any of this affects Aikman's future, it's hard to say right now. If he wants to move into a full-time front-office role, he's unlikely to earn a salary anywhere close to what he makes calling games. If he left ESPN, would the Dolphins want to make his role more permanent, especially considering his strong relationships with owner Stephen Ross and general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan? And if he's trying to set a market for his services as a broadcaster, who knows if any other network or streamer might object to the perceived conflict between the two roles.

As with so many things surrounding Troy Aikman right now, we're all waiting to see how it develops.

articles.title: NFL lifts abuse suspensions on Green Bay's Josh Jacobs and Denver's Jonathon Cooper as investigations continue
articles.summary: Josh Jacobs and Jonathon Cooper are coming off the commissioner's exempt list, but ongoing NFL investigations could bring further discipline.
articles.body: Friday was a sort of "get out of jail" day at the NFL, as Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs and Denver Broncos linebacker Jonathon Cooper learned they are coming off suspensions on the Commissioner's Exempt List. Both players have missed the start of their teams' seasons — with Cooper missing six games and Jacobs about to miss his sixth game on Sunday — because both were on the Commissioner's list in connection to domestic abuse allegations and litigation. articles.title: New Cowboys Coach Mike Pettine Explains Joining Staff Midseason, 'I Think I Can Help a Lot'
articles.summary: Former Cleveland Browns head coach Mike Pettine says he feels he can help the Dallas Cowboys "a lot" after joining the team as a senior defensive assistant ahead of Week 6.
articles.body:
Former Cleveland Browns head coach Mike Pettine says he feels he can help the Dallas Cowboys "a lot" after joining the team as a senior defensive assistant ahead of Week 6.

Pettine told reporters Friday he plans to start out by observing meetings and sitting down with first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker for one-on-one film review sessions.

"I think I can help a lot," Pettine said. "It's funny, I have about a four-inch thick book of what not to do, and a very thin one of what to do. So, I think that's key, is being able to learn from others' mistakes. As much as you think you're prepared for it, you're really not until you get into it. And I think that's where I'll be able to help him."

Tomlin's Take After Cowboys' Players-Only Meeting 💀

Parker described Pettine as someone who could serve as his "right-hand man" when speaking to reporters Thursday. Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said the same day to 105.3 The Fan he expected Pettine to report directly to him.

Past roles for Pettine included working as defensive coordinator for the New York Jets, Buffalo Bills and Green Bay Packers, where he was responsible for hiring Parker in 2019.

He most recently worked on the Minnesota Vikings' coaching staff from 2022 until coach Kevin O'Connell announced Pettine's retirement last January.

Pettine told reporters Friday he had the opportunity to accept a role with the Cowboys during spring OTAs but decided to spend time with family instead. He then received a call from Parker while recently on vacation in Italy.

"When somebody you care about reaches out, I just felt I needed to answer the call," Pettine said.

He continued, "I'm just obviously trying to hit the ground running here. I feel like I'm trying to sip water from a firehose. I'm trying to get caught up on all the film, and make observations here and there, but I'm just here to support both him and Schotty and the rest of the defensive staff any way I can."

Parker spent the past two season as passing game coordinator and defensive backs coach for the Philadelphia Eagles before he was hired to serve on Schottenheimer's defensive coordinator this offseason.

After a 2-3 start to the campaign during which the Cowboys allowed the second-most yards against in the NFL, owner Jerry Jones said on 105.3 The Fan he planned to move Parker from the sideline to the booth.

Schottenheimer said more recently on 105.3 The Fan he expected Parker to remain on the sideline while Pettine worked in the booth. The Cowboys will be testing that arrangement against one of the NFL's most effective passing attacks when kicking off Week 6 against Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers this Sunday at Lambeau Field.

articles.title: A.J. Brown, Lamar Jackson, NFL Injury Statuses and Fantasy Impact for Week 6
articles.summary: Anticipation is growing for injured fantasy football stars to return to their respective lineups.
articles.body:
Anticipation is growing for injured fantasy football stars to return to their respective lineups.

However, it might be another week until we see A.J. Brown make an impact for the New England Patriots.

Brown practiced this week and is listed as questionable, but a final decision on his Week 6 status won't be made until Saturday.

Lamar Jackson is confirmed to be sidelined for at least one more week. The Baltimore Ravens quarterback was ruled out of the clash with the Cleveland Browns due to his ankle injury.

Below is a look at all of the significant injury news affecting fantasy football lineups in Week 6.

Decision To Be Made On A.J. Brown On Saturday

Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said a final decision on A.J. Brown's Week 6 status won't be made until Saturday.

"We won't make that decision until tomorrow. We want to see how he responds to practice today and go from there," Vrabel said in his Friday press conference.

Brown has been on the injured reserve since he suffered an ankle injury in Week 1.

He has participated in practice this week, but the Patriots wanted to wait to see how Brown responded to his time on the practice field.

The Patriots might not need Brown on Sunday against the New York Jets, especially if other wide receivers step up in the same way they did in the Week 5 blowout win over the Las Vegas Raiders.

Thursday's trip to Chicago may also play a factor in the decision on Brown. A quick turnaround time between games might affect Brown's availability for the showdown with the Chicago Bears.

Demario Douglas is the Patriots wide receiver to pick up if Brown is unable to go. He had a pair of touchdowns last week against the Raiders.

Hunter Henry, who had three receptions for 44 yards and a score in Week 5, is worth a waiver-wire pickup for the FLEX spot on your roster, or if you're in need of a tight end.

Sunday's London game between the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars might be the spot to add replacements for Brown. Houston and Jacksonville both rank in the top three in receiving yards allowed to wide receivers.

Houston's Xavier Hutchinson and Jacksonville's Josh Cameron are two deep sleepers to consider if you think the game opens up for both passing games.

Lamar Jackson's ankle injury is once again keeping him out of a game.

The Ravens will go with Tyler Huntley at quarterback for the AFC North battle with the Browns.

Huntley threw for 201 yards in the Week 5 overtime win over the Atlanta Falcons. Rashod Bateman led the Ravens with 62 receiving yards.

Zay Flowers and Mark Andrews received their fair share of targets, but no pass-catcher exploded for a massive day with Huntley at the helm.

However, Josh Cuevas' two catches for 26 yards stood out. He might be a good deep sleeper at tight end if you need a player at that position due to injuries and the four teams on bye in Week 6.

C.J. Stroud, Brock Purdy and Bryce Young all face teams in the top 10 of most passing yards conceded, so they are all good options if they are available.

Cam Ward might be worth a look in place of Jackson on fantasy rosters for Week 6. The Tennessee Titans face an Indianapolis Colts defense that have allowed the fifth-most passing yards in the NFL.

articles.title: ESPN allowing Troy Aikman to walk away from Joe Buck booth would make no sense | Bobby Burack
articles.summary: Troy Aikman says ESPN has not engaged in contract negotiations with him, suggesting his departure from Monday Night Football appears most likely.
articles.body: When Joe Buck signed a $100 million extension with ESPN, the natural assumption around the industry was that Troy Aikman would soon follow. Buck and Aikman have worked together for 25 years, first at Fox and at ESPN since 2022. They are often regarded as the best broadcast booth in sports. Yet, within hours of the report about Buck's deal, industry chatter suggested that ESPN and Aikman were not close to an agreement. This week, Aikman addressed the situation — along with a reported confrontation between him and Buck during Monday Night Football — and said ESPN has not engaged in any contract negotiations with him. His deal expires in May 2027, after the Super Bowl in February that he will call. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Aikman suggested that leaving ESPN now appears to be the most likely outcome. "It just seems to be where they’re going," he said on KTCK The Ticket in Dallas. As of publication, there is still plenty of mystery surrounding why ESPN wouldn't want to keep Aikman. Yes, he's expensive. His current deal pays him around $18 million per year. ESPN, however, is paying others more, including Buck, Stephen A. Smith and Pat McAfee. As the lead NFL analyst for Monday Night Football and ESPN's first Super Bowl this February, there is an argument that Aikman is the most valuable member of that group. One industry-wide theory is that Buck wants a new partner. At the very least, Buck signing an extension before Aikman proves he is willing to work with someone else. He also apparently wasn't interested in using his leverage to ensure that he and Aikman remained together. Sources close to Buck have denied this. Another theory is that ESPN wants Peyton and Eli Manning in the booth and views this as its opportunity. However, unless the Mannings have privately agreed to such a move, which seems unlikely, pairing them with Buck sounds more like wishful thinking than an actual plan. Then there are the Kelce brothers. ESPN moved Jason Kelce into the color analyst role alongside Dave Pasch and Kurt Warner for its international games on NFL Network this season. Kelce has been polarizing, but impressive in the role. ESPN could envision eventually pairing him with his brother Travis, who is expected to retire from the NFL after this season, alongside Buck. On paper, that sounds intriguing. The problem is that there is no indication Travis is interested in becoming a full-time game analyst, much less that the Kelce brothers would be ready to anchor ESPN's most important NFL property. WITH TONY ROMO OUT AT CBS, TROY AIKMAN AND GREG OLSEN SUDDENLY BECOME LOGICAL REPLACEMENTS Greg Olsen is another possibility. He is an impending media free agent and is viewed as a potential No. 1 game analyst, a role he previously held at Fox before Tom Brady arrived. Olsen is good. Still, it's difficult to see why ESPN would prefer him to Aikman, who brings more gravitas, popularity and, most importantly, 25 years of chemistry with Buck. Sure, Olsen is 18 years younger than Aikman and would presumably cost less. If ESPN's goal were to get younger and cheaper, though, re-signing Buck — who is only two years younger than Aikman — to a nine-figure extension doesn't exactly fit that philosophy. From the outside, each alternative looks like a gamble, and probably one that wouldn't leave ESPN with a better booth than the one it already has. That's what makes the situation so puzzling. ESPN spent five years trying to find a suitable Monday Night Football booth. After Mike Tirico left in 2016 and Jon Gruden returned to coaching after the 2017 season, the network cycled through various combinations involving Steve Levy, Sean McDonough, Joe Tessitore, Booger McFarland, Brian Griese and Louis Riddick. For one reason or another, none of them clicked. And most of them are good to great broadcasters. There was even industry chatter at the time that the instability and poor reception surrounding ESPN's broadcasts affected the quality of games the NFL scheduled for Monday Night Football. For what it's worth, ESPN has enjoyed a noticeably stronger slate of games since Buck and Aikman arrived in 2022. Other factors — including ESPN's improved relationship with the NFL — undoubtedly played a role as well. Either way, ESPN finally found a booth worthy of the NFL's premier games, if not the standard for NFL broadcasting altogether, and now appears prepared to break it up. Unless there is more to the story than anyone outside the company knows, it's difficult to understand the logic. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Of course, skeptics have dismissed the entire saga as a negotiating tactic by ESPN. That doesn't appear to be the case. Usually, such tactics begin with, well, actual negotiations. According to Aikman, there haven't been any. The fact that ESPN locked up his partner before having a substantive conversation with Aikman suggests one of two things: The company has decided it doesn't want to keep him, or it hasn't decided that it does. Maybe ESPN is taking the old Bill Belichick approach with the New England Patriots: better to move on from a talent a year too early than a year too late. Maybe executives see a decline coming that viewers don't. We are skeptical.

articles.title: Commanders' K'Lavon Chaisson Makes Bold Prediction About Team's Super Bowl Hopes in Video
articles.summary: Washington Commanders outside linebacker K'Lavon Chaisson says his team hasn't given up on contending for Super Bowl LXI despite a 1-3-1 start to the 2026 season.
articles.body:
Washington Commanders outside linebacker K'Lavon Chaisson says his team hasn't given up on contending for Super Bowl LXI despite a 1-3-1 start to the 2026 season.

"I think the full belief is there," Chaisson said earlier this week (h/t DC News Now's Alex Flum ).

"I was talking to the guys, and obviously you want to go one week at a time, and focus on that, but— 13-3-1 is a weird Super Bowl-winning record, but s--t, we'll take it. Whatever it takes to get there."

Washington is heading into Week 6 ranked last in the NFC East behind three other teams that have struggled early this season in the New York Giants (3-1-1), Philadelphia Eagles (2-3-0) and Dallas Cowboys (2-3-0).

The Commanders got Jayden Daniels back from an elbow injury before Week 5, but ultimately had to settle for a tie against the New York Giants last Sunday after Daniels failed to give his team time to attempt a game-winning overtime field goal.

Daniels said Thursday he hoped to learn from the gaffe by being "more aware" when managing games going forward.

The Commanders will hope to see that lesson put into action as soon as Monday, when the team looks to begin the 12-game win streak Chaisson is hoping for against the undefeated San Francisco 49ers. Kickoff is scheduled for 8:15 p.m. ET in Santa Clara.

articles.title: KC Concepcion Defends Minkah Fitzpatrick After Concussion Despite Comments from Browns OL
articles.summary: Cleveland Browns rookie wide receiver KC Concepcion suffered a concussion last Sunday after a helmet-to-helmet hit by New York Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick during Cleveland's 17-12 road loss.
articles.body:
Cleveland Browns rookie wide receiver KC Concepcion suffered a concussion last Sunday after a helmet-to-helmet hit by New York Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick during Cleveland's 17-12 road loss.

Browns offensive lineman Dawand Jones took exception to the hit:

Concepcion, who cleared concussion protocol, practiced in full Friday and will play Sunday at home vs. the Baltimore Ravens, offered his take on the matter.

"I know the game that I signed up to play," Concepcion said Friday, via Mary Kay Cabot of cleveland.com. "This game is a very physical game. To me, it wasn't a dirty hit. It was just a football play."

Fitzpatrick received a personal foul for unnecessary roughness. Browns head coach Todd Monken also provided his thoughts on the matter.

The 22-year-old Concepcion went 24th overall in the 2026 NFL draft. The Texas A&M star has caught 18 passes (29 targets) for 149 yards through five games. He particularly excelled in a 27-24 home win over the Pittsburgh Steelers, catching five passes for a career-high 64 yards.

Concepcion is also tied for the team lead in catches with tight end Harold Fannin and running back Quinshon Judkins.

He'll be back on Sunday when the Browns host Baltimore for a crucial AFC North battle against the first-place Ravens at 1 p.m. ET.

articles.title: 49ers GM Reveals George Kittle Asked About Trade for Star Player Ahead of 2026 NFL Deadline
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle has apparently checked in on whether his team is looking to acquire veteran edge rusher Khalil Mack from the Los Angeles Chargers.
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle has apparently checked in on whether his team is looking to acquire veteran edge rusher Khalil Mack from the Los Angeles Chargers.

The subject came up when 49ers general manager John Lynch was asked in a Friday appearance on KNBR's " The Murph & Markus Show " whether he had spoken with the Chargers about Mack.

"I can't tell you that. I had a lot of people asking me that yesterday," Lynch said around the 15:30 mark of the episode (h/t 49erswebzone's David Bonilla ). "We seem to be connected to everyone. I don't know where that comes from... I had a player ask me that yesterday."

When asked to specify which player, Lynch said, "It's usually Kittle, because he asks about everything."

Mack is playing on a one-year deal without a no-trade clause, per The Athletic's Noah Furtado . The Chargers could be looking to sell ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline after an 0-5 start to the 2026 season.

The 35-year-old has recorded three sacks, 15 tackles (five for loss) and five quarterback hits during that winless start to the campaign.

Mack has appeared in six playoff games but has yet to record a postseason win in his 13-year NFL career. The undefeated 49ers could be looking for pass rush assistance should Nick Bosa miss more time with the calf injury that has sidelined him since Week 2, as well as a star to pair Bosa with down the stretch of a potential playoff run.

Whether general manager Joe Horitz shops Mack could depend at least in part on what direction his team takes over the next few weeks, although the Chargers could at best sit at 3-5 by the trade deadline.

The 49ers will for now turn their attention to Monday night's Week 6 matchup against the Washington Commanders. Bosa did not practice Thursday but has not yet been ruled out for the game.

articles.title: Eagles-Jaguars London game overrun appears to have hurt Fox, CBS pregame show viewership
articles.summary: Fox and CBS have long been frustrated by the NFL’s ever-encroaching international regular-season slate, with 9:30 a.m. ET kickoffs from Europe having the pot...
articles.body:
Fox and CBS have long been frustrated by the NFL's ever-encroaching international regular-season slate, with 9:30 a.m. ET kickoffs from Europe having the potential to deflate viewership for their pregame shows.

Those fears seemed to materialize last Sunday, thanks to a London game that started late and ran long.

Sunday's Week 5 began with the Jacksonville Jaguars taking on the Philadelphia Eagles at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London. The game, which was broadcast on NFL Network, started slowly after two players were ejected during the opening kickoff following a play that required a lengthy review. Several penalties and reviews kept it sluggish, stretching the game to almost four hours of TV time. By the time Jaguars kicker Cam Little nailed a 57-yard field goal to win, it was 1:15 p.m. ET, and the early-afternoon games on Fox and CBS were already well underway.

Awful Announcing's Drew Lerner wondered if we'd see NFL fans' pulled-focus show up in the ratings , and it certainly appears to have made an impact.

The Week 5 edition of Fox NFL Kickoff averaged 1.123 million viewers. That's the lowest figure of the season so far, though not by much, as Week 4's show garnered 1.184 million. Previous weeks averaged north of 1.4 million viewers, however, suggesting Week 4 was also likely affected by the 9:30 a.m. ET kick (Colts-Commanders in London). That international contest ended around 12:45 p.m. ET, giving viewers time to switch to the noon pregame shows before 1:00 p.m. kickoffs.

The Week 5 drop-off is far more apparant in those noon pregame shows, however.

Fox NFL Sunday drew 3.797 million viewers last Sunday, a significant drop from the previous four weeks of the NFL season. After a Week 1 debut of 4.967 million viewers, the show drew 4.854 million in Week 2, 4.541 million in Week 3, and 4.436 million in Week 4. While the show's ratings were settling after the highly anticipated season start, a 14% dip is far from normal.

The same significant drop appears in the Week 5 ratings for CBS's The NFL Today , which pulled in 2.818 million viewers last Sunday. That's an 11.5% drop from the previous week (3.183 million). That pregame show started the season with audiences of 3.654 million (Week 1), 3.375 million (Week 2), and 3.873 million (Week 3). The falloff in the last two weeks is noticeable.

What can CBS and Fox do about it? Not much, for now. They'll have to suck it up and hope for a quick turnaround in Week 6 (Texans-Jaguars in London) and Week 7 (Steelers-Saints in Paris). Following a reprieve in Week 8, another 9:30 a.m. kickoff awaits in Week 9.

Much to Fox's delight, they acquired Week 10's 9:30 a.m. kickoff from Munich (Patriots-Lions). The Week 11 Vikings-49ers game in Mexico City is a Sunday Night Football game on NBC, ending the season's international slate .

It's not all bad news for CBS either: their broadcast of the Ravens-Cowboys showdown in Brazil averaged 24.9 million viewers, the most-watched NFL International Series game in history .

So, for now, Fox and CBS will have to take the good with the bad and accept sacrificing some of their pregame audience to the NFL scheduling gods.

articles.title: George Kittle Urges 49ers To Trade For Chargers’ $18 Million Pass Rusher
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers are entering their Week 6 matchup against the Washington Commanders with a 5-0 record. The 49ers (3-0 NFC West) also hold a significa...
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers are entering their Week 6 matchup against the Washington Commanders with a 5-0 record.

The 49ers (3-0 NFC West) also hold a significant advantage in the NFC West standings. The Seattle Seahawks fell to 3-3 overall (1-1 NFC West) after their loss to the Denver Broncos on Thursday.

Meanwhile, the Los Angeles Rams hold a 2-3 record (0-1 NFC West) and are third in the division standings.

With the 49ers' early success and the Seahawks' and Rams' rocky starts, the 49ers could look to bolster their roster.

George Kittle Urges 49ers to Trade for Chargers All-Pro Pass Rusher

49ers general manager John Lynch joined Bay Area radio station KNBR on Friday. Lynch was directly asked if he is talking to the Los Angeles Chargers about star pass rusher Khalil Mack.

The 49ers GM responded, " No, I can't tell you that, but I had a lot of people ask me that yesterday."

One of those people was 49ers tight end George Kittle .

"49ers GM John Lynch said George Kittle asked him Thursday about the possibility of acquiring veteran edge Khalil Mack, who has three sacks for the 0-5 Chargers," Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area wrote on X.

In addition, Lynch gave a less-than-concrete response on KNBR when asked whether he is talking to teams ahead of the NFL trade deadline.

"Just because the flow of the trade deadline is approaching, yes. That's our job to do that, to talk with our counterparts around the league. We receive calls, we make calls, just to see where the market is at," Lynch told KNBR.

Why a Khalil Mack Trade Between the 49ers and Chargers Makes Sense?

Mack signed a 1-year, $18 million contract with the Chargers this offseason. He will be a free agent at the end of the year.

The Chargers are also having a disastrous season. Los Angeles currently holds an 0-5 record, and their schedule does not get any easier.

The AFC West could offload Mack and receive draft compensation in order to rebuild for the coming seasons.

On the other hand, the 49ers are early Super Bowl contenders after their unbeaten start. Adding a 9-time Pro Bowler to their defensive front could put San Francisco over the top.

A pass-rushing duo of Nick Bosa and Mack could become one of the best edge pairings in the NFL.

Mack has 3 sacks and 5 tackles for loss in his age-35 season.

If the Chargers are willing to move on from the edge rusher, the question becomes: what will the price tag be for the former All-Pro?

49ers Have A Long List of Injuries Along Their Defensive Line

Another reason the 49ers could look to acquire Mack is their long list of injuries along the defensive front.

San Francisco lost DT Alfred Collins to a season-ending injury before Week 1.

Defensive linemen C.J. West and Sam Okouyinonu are on injured reserve. Star edge rusher Nick Bosa could return soon from a calf injury, but he has missed the last 3 games.

articles.title: Cowboys CB Joey Porter Jr. Called Out for ‘Scam’ After Injury Update
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys get confusing injury update on star cornerback Joey Porter Jr. The post Cowboys CB Joey Porter Jr. Called Out for ‘Scam’ After Injury Update a...
articles.body:
We can all be a little suspicious of Dallas Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr.'s intentions regarding whether he wants to be on the field this year.

Especially after Porter Jr. seemingly faked a back injury as he missed the first four games with the Pittsburgh Steelers before a trade to the Cowboys — and especially after he popped up on Friday's injury report after being a full go at practice on Thursday ahead of the Week 6 primetime game against the Green Bay Packers on Sunday Night Football.

Porter Jr. is listed as questionable for the Packers game with an ankle injury. He missed a Week 5 loss to the previously winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers after arriving at the stadium and being sent home with an illness.

"Joey Porter Jr. is questionable after being limited Friday," The Athletic's Jon Machota wrote on his official X account on Friday. "He was full on Thursday."

"Joey Porter Jr. was a full participant yesterday, FWIW," The Fort Worth Star-Telegram's Joseph Hoyt wrote on his official X account on Friday.

Cowboys Executive Vice President Stephen Jones defended Porter Jr. during an appearance on 105.3-FM The Fan when asked whether he thought the son of legendary NFL linebacker Joey Porter would be all-in for the rest of the season despite not having a new contract extension — the reason he forced his way out of Pittsburgh.

"Oh, absolutely," Jones said on Friday. "I think he's all in. He wants to be out there. He was sick, he couldn't play last week with the flu. But he obviously played in our first game and I think he's fired up about what he can do to help us win against the Packers."

Steelers fans absolutely do not trust Porter Jr. — and it's hard to blame them.

"You need to be on an NFL team's active, inactive, Injured Reserve (IR), or Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list for 6 games to obtain an accrued season in the NFL," Steelers super fan Yinzer G wrote on their official X account. "Scam Porter Jr knows this. This is why he has faked a back injury, an illness and now an ankle injury. After this week he will have fully accrued enough time this season to be an unrestricted FA at the end of the year. He can just go home for the rest of the season and not have to keep doing this charade anymore. The Cowboys got played, even worse than the Steelers got played. The question is tho, what team will be stupid enough to offer him a contract next year?"

articles.title: Eagles appear set to add QB from Cowboys' practice squad as Jalen Hurts deals with blood clot
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles signed Joe Milton off the Dallas Cowboys' practice squad with Jalen Hurts sidelined indefinitely due to a blood clot.
articles.body: In the NFL, availability is often described as a player’s best ability. Since taking over as the Philadelphia Eagles’ starting quarterback, Jalen Hurts has largely embodied that idea. The Super Bowl LIX MVP started all 17 games in 2023, missed two games with a concussion in 2024 and sat out Philadelphia’s regular-season finale that year as the Eagles rested most of their starters ahead of the playoffs. Backup quarterback Tanner McKee filled in for Hurts in Week 18 to close the 2025 season and will be called upon again this Sunday. Hurts has been ruled out by what the team has described as a superficial blood clot in his calf. FORMER NFL TEAM DOCTOR ADDRESSES JALEN HURTS' BLOOD CLOT AS QB'S SEASON HINGES ON ONE KEY WORD Hurts was considered a full participant in Friday’s practice leading into this past Sunday's game against the Jacksonville Jaguars, despite dealing with a calf injury. He was not on the injury report for last week's game in London. While McKee will be QB1 this weekend, the Eagles appear to be turning to a division rival to bolster their quarterback room and potentially push rookie Cole Payton out of the backup role in Week 6. According to multiple reports, Philadelphia is set to sign Joe Milton off the Dallas Cowboys’ practice squad. Under NFL rules, any player signed from another team’s practice squad must be placed on the new team’s 53-man roster. Milton will therefore be on the active roster when the Eagles host the Carolina Panthers and look to snap their three-game losing streak. The timeline for Hurts’ return remains unclear. The Eagles did, however, release a statement detailing how the blood clot was discovered. "On Thursday, October 8th, Jalen visited the training room after practice requesting treatment for his calf," the team said. "He informed the medical staff he had been cleated during the Rams game on October 4th. This was his first treatment session for the calf injury following the game, after having practiced in full both Wednesday and Thursday. On Friday, Jalen received treatment, practiced in full, and was added to the practice report." LEGENDARY AGENT WARNS NFL TEAMS ABOUT MAKING KEY QUARTERBACK MISTAKE THAT COULD DERAIL SEASON The statement also said team doctors recommended a follow-up scan after the game. "Out of an abundance of caution, an ultrasound was performed on Saturday following the team's flight to London and walkthrough. The ultrasound revealed a superficial blood clot. Our medical staff and doctors in London reviewed the results and concluded that activity and mobility were important and that Jalen could safely play. Doctors recommended a follow-up ultrasound within 72 hours of the game and the return flight to Philadelphia." SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER Payton, a fifth-round pick in April’s draft, has appeared in just one game this season. He has yet to attempt a pass in a regular-season game. Milton has slightly more NFL experience, though he has never started a game. In limited action, he has flashed both mobility and the arm strength that made him an intriguing prospect. Sam Howell won the Cowboys' backup job during the offseason, prompting Milton’s departure from Dallas. Milton said he was surprised by the decision at the time. "It was shocking. But it's life. You got to be able to live with it and deliver blows back when it's time," he said. Milton was later added to Dallas’ practice squad, where he spent the past five weeks before the Eagles came calling Friday. It remains unclear what the Eagles’ decision to add a quarterback signals about Hurts’ status or whether they expect him to miss an extended period. articles.title: Caleb Williams Hints at Injury Return, Reposts Hype Video to TikTok Before Bears vs. Falcons
articles.summary: Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams is seemingly hinting he plans to return from injury this Sunday for a Week 6 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons.
articles.body:
Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams is seemingly hinting he plans to return from injury this Sunday for a Week 6 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons.

Williams, who has been sidelined since Week 2, reposted an edit on his TikTok account which showed footage of the quarterback being carted off the field set to audio mocking his reaction to his hamstring injury.

The video then showed a clip indicating the quarterback had "flipped a switch" before transitioning into a Williams highlight reel.

Williams was listed as questionable for Sunday's game on the Bears' Friday injury report.
